turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Morning. Have a seat there. What's the problem?
[SEG0002] person_2 (CAREGIVER): She's destroyed with the tiredness, doctor.
[SEG0007] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Asleep in the chair after the dinner. I'm her carer, in three mornings a week. The M50 was a pure nightmare getting in, mind.
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): Even with the heat on?
[SEG0012] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Two jumpers on her and the hands are still perishing.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Can you date the start?
[SEG0017] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Um, last winter, or the one before. She can't say. I'd put it nearer two years.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): So months from yourself, two years from the carer. We won't fix the date today.
[SEG0021] person_2 (CAREGIVER): A stone... ah no, a stone and a half. The good trousers won't fasten.
[SEG0026] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Every three or four days. Lactulose, fifteen mils twice a day... no, thirty mils, once at night. She stopped it.
[SEG0028] person_2 (CAREGIVER): March. No, April, after Easter. Useless yoke.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Did you take the iron tablets they prescribed?
[SEG0031] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Never collected them from the chemist.
[SEG0036] person_2 (CAREGIVER): She says it's the work and her age. Office job, long hours. She's fifty-two.
[SEG0047] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Underactive thyroid, on the tablets for years. She's dead now, Lord rest her.
[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): Thyroid blood test yourself, ever?
[SEG0051] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Sorry, I'm mixing her up with the mammy. Borderline was her mother's. She had a test once, years ago, thought it was grand. No date on it.
[SEG0054] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll check the neck. Thyroid's not enlarged. Hands are cool. Pulse sixty-eight... no, seventy-two, and regular.

[SEG0055] person_1 (DOCTOR): Tired, cold, weight up, constipated, flat mood, and the mother had thyroid disease. Could be an underactive thyroid, could be iron deficiency. I won't conclude which today.

[SEG0056] person_1 (DOCTOR): Bloods today: thyroid function, full blood count, and ferritin. Back here in a fortnight for the results. Fibre and fluids in the meantime, and no thyroid tablets unless I start them.
[SEG0057] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Grand. We'll get the bloods done on the way out.

spec.situation: Middle-aged person tired and cold for months, weight up, constipated, low mood; pins it on work and age; mother had thyroid disease; one old thyroid test result recalled wrongly ('borderline, they said'). Blood test planned.
features: vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.

doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.
self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.

bad.reason: Tiredness and duration uncertainty supported; 'reported_by=patient' incomplete because caregiver also reported duration.
bad.text: Tiredness (category=constitutional, status=present, duration=approximately several months to 2 years, temporality=current, reported_by=patient, certainty=uncertain)

bad.reason: Date uncertainty supported, but 'patient saying last winter or winter before' was caregiver, not patient.
bad.text: The patient cannot date the start of the tiredness, saying last winter or the winter before. (type=date_uncertain, related_entities=symptoms[0], resolution_status=unresolved)

omissions.text: Feeling cold is worse even with the heat on, and caregiver reports hands are still perishing despite two jumpers.
Tiredness is all day, with caregiver noting she falls asleep in the chair after dinner.
Constipation detail from patient: not opening bowels every day.
Lactulose history is inconsistent/uncertain: caregiver first said 15 mL twice a day, then corrected to 30 mL once at night.
Lactulose was stopped after Easter in April because it was ineffective.
Iron tablets had been prescribed previously but were never collected from the pharmacy and therefore not taken.
Low mood was characterized as feeling 'flat' rather than weepy.
Age recorded in conversation: 52 years old.

Previous thyroid blood test history is uncertain/corrected: caregiver initially confused the mother's 'borderline' result with the patient; patient herself had a thyroid test once years ago that was thought to be normal.
Pulse was initially stated as 68 then corrected to 72 bpm, regular.
